title: Efficient Fault-Tolerant Single Qubit Gate Approximation And Universal Quantum Computation Without Using The Solovay-Kit

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract says the challenge is to approximate using 'Ω(log[1/ϵ]) gates'; Ω denotes a lower bound, not an achievable gate count. The Introduction correctly states the lower bound and asks whether it can be attained, so the abstract should say O(log[1/ϵ]), not Ω.

The paper claims a partial answer but allows a gate set that depends on ϵ: 'chosen from a finite set depending on the value of ϵ'. The Nielsen-Chuang challenge is for a fixed finite set independent of ϵ. A set whose size/identity changes with ϵ is not a fixed finite set, so this does not answer the stated challenge.

The conclusion states the gate count as 'O(ϵ log[1/ϵ] log log[1/ϵ] ···)'. This contains a spurious factor ϵ; as ϵ→0 the complexity would decrease, which is impossible for higher accuracy. It contradicts the abstract's O(log[1/ϵ] log log...).

The paper defines 'm = ⌈ϵ/ [log_2(1/ϵ) log_2 log_2(1/ϵ)···]⌉'. This is inverted: for small ϵ this tends to 1, whereas to approximate to accuracy ϵ one needs m ≈ log_2(1/ϵ)+... . With m=1 the set cannot approximate arbitrary phase gates.

It says to make each phase gate 'accurate to ϵ log_2(1/ϵ) log_2 log_2(1/ϵ)···'. As written, the angle error is multiplied by the log product, i.e. larger than ϵ, which would not guarantee total error ≤ ϵ. It should be ϵ divided by the product. This also contradicts the earlier δ ≤ ϵ/⌈log_2(1/ϵ)⌉.

The paper sets w_j=δ_{jℓ} only for ℓ=1,...,n−2k, but w is in R^{n−k}. If H=[L|G], the remaining k components corresponding to the G block must be set to zero for v to be orthogonal to the classical code C. Without specifying them, an arbitrary solution v need not satisfy the phase-stabilizer condition, so Eq. (4) is not valid as stated.

predicted_errors.error_location: Method, 'Now I report how to execute P(2α)_L'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says the gate-teleportation circuit executes P(2α)_L, but the same paragraph says that for α=π/4 the circuit is used to execute the T gate. Since T=P(π/4)=P(α), the circuit with ancilla |Θ(α)> and correction P(2α) executes P(α), not P(2α).

The statement that logical Z, H, X, S and CNOT are automatically FT for any Steane-like CSS code is overbroad: transversal S does not generally implement logical S for arbitrary self-orthogonal codes. Their own Eq. (4) may require physical rotations such as P(α/2) rather than S, depending on the code.

The operator 'P(α)_L X_L P(−α)_L' is not a stabilizer as written: it has eigenvalue e^{iα} on |Θ(α)>_L and is not Hermitian with ±1 eigenvalues. One must include the global phase e^{-iα/2} to make it a Hermitian ±1 stabilizer.
The text refers to Fig. 1 and Fig. 2, but the embedded figures are labelled Figure 0 and Figure 1, and no Figure 2 is present. This is an off-by-one figure-numbering inconsistency.

The final gate set restricts to ℓ<2^m, giving angles πℓ/2^m in [0,π). But the preceding approximation condition |α−πℓ/2^m|<δ for α∈(0,2π) requires ℓ up to about 2^{m+1}. The stated set therefore does not cover all phase gates on the full circle.

For a general Steane-like code, the real solution v to Hv=e_ℓ can have non-dyadic rational entries, so the physical gates P(α v_j) are not necessarily in the claimed finite set {H, P(πℓ/2^m)}. The paper does not restrict to codes such as the Steane code where v_j are integers, so the claimed gate set is insufficient for the general construction.
